1	I have three background jobs pending (the confirmation build, the janitor, and the reviewer) and shouldn't start new Lean work I can't verify before they land. Let me summarize where things stand.
2	
3	**What I found and changed**
4	
5	The representability lane had been stuck for ~7 sessions on a hypothesis it never needed. The DD-R certificate assembler demanded a *global* certificate `IsCertified g` over the carve chart ring, whose no-leak input is genuinely false for refined pieces (recorded as memory I-0209, and read for months as "the lane is blocked"). But every downstream consumer goes through `DivFamZar`, whose predicate is the *Zariski-local* `IsLocallyCertified` — a span-⊤ family of base localizations each carrying an ordinary certificate. The impossibility ruled out one spelling of the goal, not the goal.
6	
7	The distinction that matters: localizing the **pieces** destroys finiteness (I-0209 is right about that), but localizing the **base** keeps the divisor scheme finite over it, and that is exactly what the consumer predicate is built from.
8	
9	**Landed, all kernel-checked** (`lake env lean`, warning-free, axioms only `propext`/`Classical.choice`/`Quot.sound`):
10	
11	- the span-⊤ production rule for `IsLocallyCertified`, and a **pointwise** gate via quasi-compactness of `Spec R` — an away-certificate at each prime suffices;
12	- an adaptation-free form (the adaptation is free by extraction, so only the certificate over the shrunken base remains);
13	- the support tube refined to `Away`-chart form, plus the no-leak clause derived from support containment — so the previously false hypothesis becomes true over the tube;
14	- the invented spanning submodule eliminated from both assemblers;
15	- the F5 forward map weakened to take a `DivFamZar` class, with agreement to the old map by `rfl` — proving the certificate argument it demanded was definitionally unused. Without this the forward direction would have re-imposed the gate I'd just removed.
16	
17	Two audits worth flagging: `DivRepGlobalData.representableBy` already delivers the `divRep` endpoint from clauses stated purely on `divFamZar`, and `DivFamZar.exists_certChartCover` already extracts away-local certified representatives — so the away-local shape is this lane's own currency, not a workaround.
18	
19	**Roadmap**: the opaque certificate blocker is now four leaves — `zar-gate` done, and `tube-fibre` / `away-kerspan` / `away-assemble` pending, each reduced to a named fibrewise fact. The degree input was already proved last session.
20	
21	**Honest caveats**: the two remaining certificate obligations are real geometry, not packaging — and the syzygy file proves the kernel-spanning one is *equivalent* to the flatness being sought, so no cleverer submodule choice will evade it. The objective is not complete. A confirmation `lake build` of the kerspan module and two review agents are still running; I'll fold in their results when they land.

16	fibre analyses all read at a single `p : PrimeSpectrum R`.
17	
18	This file closes that gap with the quasi-compactness step.  If for every prime `p` there
19	is some `r ∉ p` over whose away localization the system is certified, then the good
20	elements span the unit ideal (their basic opens cover `Spec R`), so finitely many of them
21	already do — and `isLocallyCertified_of_forall_exists_away` applies.
22	
23	The result is that the certificate gate for the DD-R endgame is now genuinely *pointwise*:
24	one base point at a time, exactly the shape the landed fibre machinery delivers.
25	
26	## Main declarations
27	
28	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_away` — the pointwise gate
29	  for a bare local-equation system.
30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ThetaGeneratorSeed.isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_away_certified`
31	  — the seed form.
32	-/

48	section SpanTop
49	
50	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
51	
52	/-- **Pointwise good elements span the unit ideal, finitely.** If a predicate `P` on `R`
53	holds at some element outside each prime, then finitely many elements satisfying `P` span
54	`⊤`.  This is quasi-compactness of `Spec R` in the elementary form the certificate gate
55	needs: the basic opens of the good elements cover the spectrum, hence the good set spans
56	the unit ideal, hence `1` is a finite combination of good elements. -/
57	theorem exists_fin_span_eq_top_of_forall_prime (P : R → Prop)
58	    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, ∃ r, r ∉ p.asIdeal ∧ P r) :
59	    ∃ (m : ℕ) (g : Fin m → R), Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤ ∧ ∀ i, P (g i) := by
60	  classical
61	  -- the good elements span the unit ideal, because their basic opens cover `Spec R`
62	  have hspan : Ideal.span {r : R | P r} = ⊤ := by
63	    rw [← PrimeSpectrum.iSup_basicOpen_eq_top_iff']
64	    refine top_le_iff.mp fun p _ => ?_
65	    obtain ⟨r, hrp, hrP⟩ := h p
66	    exact Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨r, by
67	      simpa only [Opens.mem_iSup, PrimeSpectrum.mem_basicOpen] using ⟨hrP, hrp⟩⟩
68	  -- `1` is then a finite combination of good elements
69	  have hone : (1 : R) ∈ Submodule.span R {r : R | P r} := by
70	    show (1 : R) ∈ Ideal.span {r : R | P r}
71	    rw [hspan]; exact Submodule.mem_top
72	  obtain ⟨T, hTsub, hT⟩ := Submodule.mem_span_finite_of_mem_span hone
73	  refine ⟨T.card, fun i => (T.equivFin.symm i : R), ?_, fun i => hTsub (T.equivFin.symm i).2⟩
74	  have hrange : Set.range (fun i : Fin T.card => ((T.equivFin.symm i : R))) = (T : Set R) := by
75	    ext x
76	    constructor
77	    · rintro ⟨i, rfl⟩
78	      exact (T.equivFin.symm i).2
79	    · intro hx
80	      exact ⟨T.equivFin ⟨x, hx⟩, by simp⟩
81	  rw [hrange]
82	  exact Ideal.eq_top_of_isUnit_mem _ hT isUnit_one
83	
84	end SpanTop

94	/-- **The pointwise certificate gate.** If over every prime of the base there is an away
95	localization carrying a certified family divisor-equal to the pulled system, the system is
96	locally certified.  Combines the quasi-compactness step with the span-`⊤` production rule
97	`isLocallyCertified_of_forall_exists_away`. -/
98	theorem isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_away {n : ℕ}
99	    {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
100	    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, ∃ r, r ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
101	      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) :=
102	        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away r) r
103	      ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C (Localization.Away r) pi n,
104	        Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns
105	          (d.pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r))
106	            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
107	              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) d))) :
108	    IsLocallyCertified C R pi n d := by
109	  obtain ⟨m, g, hg, hgood⟩ := exists_fin_span_eq_top_of_forall_prime
110	    (fun r =>
111	      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) :=
112	        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away r) r
113	      ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C (Localization.Away r) pi n,
114	        Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns
115	          (d.pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r))
116	            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
117	              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) d))) h
118	  exact isLocallyCertified_of_forall_exists_away g hg hgood
119	
120	end Pointwise

124	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} [IsProper C.hom]
125	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
126	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R] [IsNoetherianRing R]

132	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

134	/-- **The pointwise certificate gate for a seed.** One base point at a time: an away
135	localization at each prime carrying a certified family divisor-equal to the pulled seed
136	system makes the seed's system locally certified, hence a `DivFamZar` class.
137	
138	This is the shape the landed geometry actually produces — the support tube isolates pieces
139	over a neighbourhood of one base point, and every fibre analysis reads at a single prime —
140	so no globally valid no-leak hypothesis (false in general, I-0209) is required anywhere. -/
141	theorem isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_away_certified (hD : D.IsGenerator)
142	    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, ∃ r, r ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
143	      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) :=
144	        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away r) r
145	      ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C (Localization.Away r) pi n,
146	        Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns
147	          ((D.localEquations hD).pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r))
148	            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
149	              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) (D.localEquations hD)))) :
150	    IsLocallyCertified C R pi n (D.localEquations hD) :=
151	  isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_away h
152	
153	/-- **The gate in its most consumable form: certify the pulled system after shrinking.**
154	At every prime it suffices to produce an `r ∉ p` and a certificate for *some* adaptation
155	of the pulled seed system over `Localization.Away r`.  The adaptation itself is free
156	(`exists_divisorAdaptation`), so the only genuine obligation is the certificate over the
157	shrunken base — where the support tube makes per-piece isolation available.
158	
159	Contrast with the old gate `divisorAdaptation_isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning`,
160	which demanded a certificate for the *canonically extracted* adaptation over the whole
161	chart ring; that shape forces a globally valid no-leak hypothesis, which is false. -/
162	theorem isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_certified_adaptation
163	    (hD : D.IsGenerator)
164	    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, ∃ r, r ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
165	      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) :=
166	        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away r) r
167	      ∃ A : DivisorAdaptation C (Localization.Away r) pi
168	          ((D.localEquations hD).pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r))
169	            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
170	              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) (D.localEquations hD))),
171	        A.IsCertified n) :
172	    IsLocallyCertified C R pi n (D.localEquations hD) := by
173	  refine isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_away_certified hD fun p => ?_
174	  obtain ⟨r, hrp, A, hA⟩ := h p
175	  haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) :=
176	    isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away r) r
177	  -- bundle the supplied adaptation and its certificate; the divisor equality is `rfl`
178	  exact ⟨r, hrp, ⟨_, A, hA⟩, Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_refl _⟩
179	
180	/-- The `DivFamZar` class of a seed certified pointwise on the base. -/
181	noncomputable def divFamZar_of_forall_prime_away_certified (hD : D.IsGenerator)
182	    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, ∃ r, r ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
183	      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) :=
184	        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away r) r
185	      ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C (Localization.Away r) pi n,
186	        Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns
187	          ((D.localEquations hD).pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r))
188	            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
189	              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) (D.localEquations hD)))) :
190	    DivFamZar C R pi n :=
191	  DivFamZar.mk (D.localEquations hD)
192	    (isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_away_certified hD h)
193	
194	end ThetaGeneratorSeed

10	/-!
11	# The support tube in `Away`-chart form
12	
13	The pointwise certificate gate (`DivSchemeCertZarPointwise.lean`) asks, at each base prime
14	`p`, for an element `r ∉ p` such that the pulled system is certified over
15	`Localization.Away r`.  The support tube (`Scheme.LocalEquations.exists_supportTube`)
16	delivers piece isolation over an *abstract* Zariski neighbourhood `V` of `p`.  This file
17	refines that neighbourhood to a basic open — the shape `Localization.Away` needs — and
18	records the resulting statement.
19	
20	The refinement is the standard fact that basic opens form a topological basis of
21	`Spec R` (`PrimeSpectrum.isBasis_basic_opens`); the content is only that the tube's
22	conclusion is monotone in the neighbourhood, so shrinking `V` to a basic open inside it
23	preserves support isolation.
24	
25	## Main declarations
26	
27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.exists_basicOpen_supportTube` — the tube with a
28	  basic-open neighbourhood: an `r ∉ p` whose basic open isolates the support inside `U`.
29	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_notMem_supportLocus_subset_of_fibre` — the same for the
30	  relative curve over a test ring, with the properness licence supplied.
31	-/
32	
33	set_option autoImplicit false
34	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

39	
40	namespace AlgebraicGeometry

44	namespace Scheme.LocalEquations
45	
46	variable {X : Scheme.{u}} {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (d : X.LocalEquations)
47	
48	/-- **The support tube with a basic-open neighbourhood.** If the support fibre over a base
49	prime `p` lies inside an open `U`, then some `r ∉ p` has its whole basic-open preimage's
50	support inside `U`.
51	
52	The tube produces an abstract neighbourhood; basic opens are a basis of `Spec R`
53	(`PrimeSpectrum.isBasis_basic_opens`), so shrinking to a basic open inside it keeps the
54	conclusion by monotonicity of the preimage. This is the form the `Localization.Away`
55	charts of `IsLocallyCertified` consume. -/
56	theorem exists_basicOpen_supportTube (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of R))
57	    [UniversallyClosed f] {U : Set X} (hU : IsOpen U) {p : PrimeSpectrum R}
58	    (hfib : f.base ⁻¹' {(p : Spec (CommRingCat.of R))} ∩ d.supportLocus ⊆ U) :
59	    ∃ r : R, r ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
60	      f.base ⁻¹' (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen r : Set (PrimeSpectrum R))
61	        ∩ d.supportLocus ⊆ U := by
62	  obtain ⟨V, hpV, hV⟩ := d.exists_supportTube f hU hfib
63	  -- refine `V` to a basic open around `p`
64	  obtain ⟨W, hWmem, hpW, hWV⟩ :=
65	    PrimeSpectrum.isTopologicalBasis_basic_opens.exists_subset_of_mem_open
66	      (a := p) hpV V.isOpen
67	  obtain ⟨r, rfl⟩ := hWmem
68	  exact ⟨r, (PrimeSpectrum.mem_basicOpen r p).mp hpW,
69	    fun x hx => hV ⟨hWV hx.1, hx.2⟩⟩
70	
71	end Scheme.LocalEquations

73	/-! ## The relative-curve form -/
74	
75	section RelCurve
76	
77	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
78	variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
79	
80	/-- **The relative-curve support tube, basic-open form.** For a local-equation system on
81	the relative curve over a test ring, fibrewise containment of the support in an open `U`
82	at a prime `p` gives an `r ∉ p` isolating the support over the basic open of `r`.
83	
84	The properness licence is `instIsProperRelCurveHom`; `UniversallyClosed` fires by
85	resolution. -/
86	theorem exists_notMem_supportLocus_subset_of_fibre
87	    (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) {U : Set (relCurve C R)} (hU : IsOpen U)
88	    {p : PrimeSpectrum R}
89	    (hfib : ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).base ⁻¹'
90	        {(p : Spec (CommRingCat.of R))} ∩ d.supportLocus ⊆ U) :
91	    ∃ r : R, r ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
92	      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).base ⁻¹'
93	          (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen r : Set (PrimeSpectrum R))
94	        ∩ d.supportLocus ⊆ U :=
95	  d.exists_basicOpen_supportTube _ hU hfib

99	/-! ## No-leak over a shrunken base, from one fibre
100	
101	The point of the tube in the certificate lane: the no-leak hypothesis that is false
102	globally becomes *true over the tube*, because the support over the tube is already inside
103	the piece — so its closure is too, and the fibre clause holds for every base point of the
104	tube rather than only the one it was checked at. -/
105	
106	section NoLeakOverTube
107	
108	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} [IsProper C.hom]
109	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
110	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom pi]
111	variable {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
112	
113	namespace DivisorAdaptation
114	
115	variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R pi d)
116	
117	omit [IsProper C.hom]
118	
119	/-- **Support containment upgrades to the fibrewise no-leak clause.** If the whole family
120	support lies in the piece `j`, then over every base point the fibre of the *closure* of the
121	piece trace stays in the piece: the trace is then all of the support, which is closed.
122	
123	This is the bridge between what the tube delivers (support containment over a shrunken
124	base) and what the certificate assembler consumes (the fibrewise clause of
125	`finite_colength_of_forall_fibre_closure_subset`). -/
126	theorem forall_fibre_closure_subset_of_supportLocus_subset (j : A.index)
127	    (hsub : d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
128	    ∀ s : Spec (CommRingCat.of R),
129	      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).base ⁻¹' {s}
130	          ∩ closure (d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)))
131	        ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)) := by
132	  intro s x hx
133	  have htrace : d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)) = d.supportLocus :=
134	    Set.inter_eq_left.mpr hsub
135	  rw [htrace, d.isClosed_supportLocus.closure_eq] at hx
136	  exact hsub hx.2
137	
138	/-- The no-leak clause for **every** piece, from containment of the support in each: the
139	exact `hnoLeak` input of the certificate assemblers
140	(`DivisorAdaptation.isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning`,
141	`ThetaGeneratorSeed.divisorAdaptation_isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning`). -/
142	theorem forall_noLeak_of_forall_supportLocus_subset
143	    (hsub : ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
144	    ∀ (j : A.index) (s : Spec (CommRingCat.of R)),
145	      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).base ⁻¹' {s}
146	          ∩ closure (d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)))
147	        ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)) :=
148	  fun j => A.forall_fibre_closure_subset_of_supportLocus_subset j (hsub j)
149	
150	end DivisorAdaptation
151	
152	end NoLeakOverTube

154	/-! ## The tube-fibre reduction
155	
156	Combining the two halves: to obtain the certificate assembler's `hnoLeak` input over an
157	`Away` chart, it is enough to check at ONE base prime that the support fibre lies in an
158	open — the tube spreads it to a basic-open neighbourhood, and containment there upgrades to
159	the fibrewise clause. This is the precise statement the remaining geometric work has to
160	feed, and it mentions only a single fibre. -/
161	
162	section TubeFibre
163	
164	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
165	variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
166	
167	/-- **The tube-fibre reduction.** If at a base prime `p` the support fibre of the system
168	lies inside an open `U`, then some `r ∉ p` has the entire support over `D(r)` inside `U`.
169	
170	Stated so that the remaining certificate obligation is *purely fibrewise*: check one fibre,
171	get a Zariski chart.  The consumer chain is
172	`exists_notMem_supportLocus_subset_of_fibre` → the pulled system's support over `D(r)` →
173	`DivisorAdaptation.forall_noLeak_of_forall_supportLocus_subset` → the assembler's
174	`hnoLeak`, and then `isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_certified_adaptation`
175	consumes the resulting away-certificate. -/
176	theorem exists_away_supportLocus_subset_of_fibre_subset
177	    (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) (U : (relCurve C R).Opens) {p : PrimeSpectrum R}
178	    (hfib : ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).base ⁻¹'
179	        {(p : Spec (CommRingCat.of R))} ∩ d.supportLocus ⊆ (U : Set (relCurve C R))) :
180	    ∃ r : R, r ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
181	      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).base ⁻¹'
182	          (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen r : Set (PrimeSpectrum R)) ∩ d.supportLocus
183	        ⊆ (U : Set (relCurve C R)) :=
184	  exists_notMem_supportLocus_subset_of_fibre C R d U.isOpen hfib
185	
186	end TubeFibre

10	/-!
11	# The certificate's kernel-spanning input, with the submodule eliminated
12	
13	The certificate assemblers take a submodule `L ≤ ker (δ_left − δ_right)` together with the
14	fibrewise-spanning law `hspan`.  Choosing `L` is not where the difficulty lies: the
15	canonical choice `L = ker (δ_left − δ_right)` always satisfies `hle` by `le_rfl`, and for
16	that choice `hspan` is *equivalent* to residue-fibre injectivity of the injectivized map
17	(`ker_rTensor_le_range_subtype_iff_liftQ_rTensor_injective`).
18	
19	This file records the resulting assembler interfaces, which mention no submodule at all.
20	It is a packaging step, not a weakening: the remaining content is the fibre injectivity,
21	which the syzygy file already shows is equivalent to the flat-cokernel clause and so
22	genuinely needs relative geometry (it is not evadable by a cleverer choice of `L`).
23	
24	Combined with `DivSchemeCertZarTube.lean`, the certificate obligation over an `Away` chart
25	is now exactly two fibrewise facts: support containment in a piece, and injectivity of the
26	injectivized Čech difference on each residue fibre.
27	
28	## Main declarations
29	
30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.isCertified_of_noLeak_of_forall_liftQ_injective` —
31	  the assembler with `L` eliminated.
32	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ThetaGeneratorSeed.divisorAdaptation_isCertified_of_noLeak_liftQ_degree`
33	  — the seed form, with the degree input in the landed pulled-divisor spelling.
34	-/

54	variable {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
55	variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R pi d)
56	
57	/-- **The assembler with the spanning submodule eliminated.** Taking `L` to be the actual
58	kernel of the Čech difference makes `hle` trivial and turns `hspan` into residue-fibre
59	injectivity of the injectivized map — so the certificate needs no invented submodule.
60	
61	The remaining hypothesis `hinj` is genuine relative content: the syzygy file proves it
62	equivalent to the flat-cokernel clause, hence not evadable by choosing `L` differently. -/

119	of the (c1)-finite clause: if over every base point the fibre of the closure of the
120	trace stays inside `U`, the leak locus is empty.  In the CertUniv instantiation the
121	hypothesis is produced from the seed design and the P-fib-N fibre analysis (the fibre
122	support is a finite set of pairwise-incomparable closed points, each isolated inside
123	its piece). -/
124	lemma supportLeak_eq_empty_of_forall_fibre (f : X ⟶ S) {U : X.Opens}
125	    (hfib : ∀ s : S, f.base ⁻¹' {s} ∩ closure (d.supportLocus ∩ (U : Set X))
126	      ⊆ (U : Set X)) :
127	    d.supportLeak U = ∅ := by
128	  rw [Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem]
129	  rintro x ⟨hxc, hxU⟩
130	  exact hxU (hfib (f.base x) ⟨rfl, hxc⟩)
131

133	(the properness licence): its complement is the Zariski-open locus of the base over
134	which the support trace on `U` is closed — the tube-side mechanism for producing the
135	closed-trace input Zariski-locally on the base. -/
136	theorem isClosed_image_supportLeak (f : X ⟶ S) [UniversallyClosed f] (U : X.Opens) :
137	    IsClosed (f.base '' d.supportLeak U) :=
138	  f.isClosedMap _ (d.isClosed_supportLeak U)
139	
140	end Scheme.LocalEquations

142	/-! ## The abstract finiteness engine -/
143	
144	namespace IsAffineOpen
145	
146	variable {X : Scheme.{u}} {V : X.Opens} (hV : IsAffineOpen V)
147	
148	/-- The underlying set of the closed subscheme of an affine open cut by an ideal of its
149	section ring, embedded in the ambient scheme: `Spec (Γ(X, V) ⧸ I) ⟶ Spec Γ(X, V) ⟶ X`
150	has range the vanishing set of `I` on `V`. -/
151	lemma range_specMap_quotient_mk_fromSpec (I : Ideal Γ(X, V)) :
152	    Set.range ⇑(Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)) ≫ hV.fromSpec)
153	      = X.zeroLocus (I : Set Γ(X, V)) ∩ (V : Set X) := by
154	  have hcomp : ⇑(Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)) ≫ hV.fromSpec)
155	      = ⇑hV.fromSpec ∘ ⇑(Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))) := by
156	    ext x
157	    exact Scheme.Hom.comp_apply _ _ x
158	  have hq : Set.range ⇑(Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)))
159	      = PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set Γ(X, V)) := by
160	    have h := range_comap_of_surjective _ _ (Ideal.Quotient.mk_surjective (I := I))
161	    rw [Ideal.mk_ker] at h
162	    exact h
163	  rw [hcomp, Set.range_comp, hq]
164	  exact hV.fromSpec_image_zeroLocus _
165	
166	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of R))]
167	
168	/-- **The structure triangle of the chart-local closed subscheme**: composing
169	`Spec (Γ(X, V) ⧸ I) ⟶ X` with the structure morphism is `Spec` of the structure map
170	`R → Γ(X, V) ⧸ I` (the `Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra` algebra, quotient structure). -/
171	lemma specMap_quotient_mk_fromSpec_over (I : Ideal Γ(X, V)) :
172	    Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)) ≫ hV.fromSpec
173	        ≫ (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R))
174	      = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R (Γ(X, V) ⧸ I))) := by
175	  have h1 : hV.fromSpec ≫ (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R))
176	      = Spec.map ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of R)).inv
177	          ≫ (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).appLE ⊤ V le_top) := by
178	    have h2 := (SpecMap_appLE_fromSpec (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R))
179	      (isAffineOpen_top (Spec (CommRingCat.of R))) hV le_top).symm
180	    rw [IsAffineOpen.fromSpec_top, Scheme.isoSpec_Spec_inv, ← Spec.map_comp] at h2
181	    exact h2

183	      = ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of R)).inv
184	          ≫ (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).appLE ⊤ V le_top)
185	        ≫ CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) := by
186	    have happ : X.overAlgebraMap R V
187	        = ((X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).appLE ⊤ V le_top).hom.comp
188	          (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of R)).inv.hom := by
189	      rw [Scheme.overAlgebraMap, CommRingCat.hom_comp]
190	      rfl
191	    have hmk : algebraMap R (Γ(X, V) ⧸ I)
192	        = (Ideal.Quotient.mk I).comp (X.overAlgebraMap R V) := by
193	      rw [← Scheme.algebraMap_overSectionsAlgebra, Ideal.Quotient.mk_comp_algebraMap]
194	    ext r
195	    simp only [CommRingCat.hom_ofHom, hmk, happ, RingHom.comp_apply,
196	      CommRingCat.hom_comp]
197	  rw [h1, ← Spec.map_comp, halg]
198	
199	include hV in
200	/-- **Ideal-valued support finiteness.**  If the closed subscheme cut out by an
201	arbitrary ideal `I` on an affine open `V` has closed image in the proper ambient
202	scheme, then its coordinate ring is finite over the base.  This is the
203	non-principal form needed for chart-reading ideals; the proof is the same
204	universally-closed affine-morphism argument as the principal engine below. -/
205	theorem finite_quotient_of_isClosed
206	    [UniversallyClosed (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R))]
207	    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R))]
208	    (I : Ideal Γ(X, V))
209	    (hclosed : IsClosed (X.zeroLocus (I : Set Γ(X, V)) ∩ (V : Set X))) :
210	    Module.Finite R (Γ(X, V) ⧸ I) := by
211	  haveI hci : IsClosedImmersion
212	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)) ≫ hV.fromSpec) :=
213	    IsClosedImmersion.of_isPreimmersion _
214	      ((hV.range_specMap_quotient_mk_fromSpec I) ▸ hclosed)
215	  have hfin : IsFinite ((Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)) ≫
216	      hV.fromSpec) ≫ (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R))) := by
217	    rw [IsFinite.iff_isIntegralHom_and_locallyOfFiniteType,
218	      IsIntegralHom.iff_universallyClosed_and_isAffineHom]
219	    exact ⟨⟨inferInstance, inferInstance⟩, inferInstance⟩
220	  rw [Category.assoc, hV.specMap_quotient_mk_fromSpec_over] at hfin
221	  exact RingHom.finite_algebraMap.mp ((IsFinite.SpecMap_iff _).mp hfin)
222	
223	include hV in
224	/-- **The abstract (c1)-finiteness engine** (Kleiman's finiteness of the divisor
225	subscheme, chart-local form): for an affine open `V` of a scheme `X` over `Spec R`
226	whose structure morphism is universally closed and locally of finite type, and a
227	section `g` whose non-vanishing complement `V \ D(g)` is CLOSED in `X`, the quotient
228	`Γ(X, V) ⧸ (g)` is a finite `R`-module.
229	
230	Route: `Spec (Γ(X, V) ⧸ (g)) ⟶ X` is a preimmersion with closed range, hence a closed
231	immersion; composing with the structure morphism is universally closed, affine (a
232	morphism of affine schemes) and locally of finite type, hence integral
233	(`IsIntegralHom.iff_universallyClosed_and_isAffineHom`) and finite
234	(`IsFinite.iff_isIntegralHom_and_locallyOfFiniteType`); the composite IS `Spec` of the
235	structure map (`specMap_quotient_mk_fromSpec_over`), so `IsFinite.SpecMap_iff` reads
236	off `RingHom.Finite`.  No Noetherian hypothesis.  The universal-closedness input
237	excludes the affine-line guard example; the closedness input excludes the hyperbola
238	and leaking-piece guards (file header). -/
239	theorem finite_quotient_span_singleton_of_isClosed
240	    [UniversallyClosed (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R))]
241	    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R))]
242	    (g : Γ(X, V))
243	    (hclosed : IsClosed ((V : Set X) \ (X.basicOpen g : Set X))) :
244	    Module.Finite R (Γ(X, V) ⧸ Ideal.span {g}) := by
245	  have hrange : Set.range ⇑(Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
246	      (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {g}))) ≫ hV.fromSpec)
247	      = (V : Set X) \ (X.basicOpen g : Set X) := by
248	    rw [hV.range_specMap_quotient_mk_fromSpec, Scheme.zeroLocus_span]
249	    ext x
250	    simp only [Set.mem_inter_iff, Scheme.mem_zeroLocus_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff,
251	      forall_eq, Set.mem_sdiff, SetLike.mem_coe]
252	    exact and_comm
253	  haveI hci : IsClosedImmersion
254	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {g})))
255	        ≫ hV.fromSpec) :=
256	    IsClosedImmersion.of_isPreimmersion _ (hrange ▸ hclosed)
257	  have hfin : IsFinite ((Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
258	      (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {g}))) ≫ hV.fromSpec)
259	        ≫ (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R))) := by
260	    rw [IsFinite.iff_isIntegralHom_and_locallyOfFiniteType,
261	      IsIntegralHom.iff_universallyClosed_and_isAffineHom]
262	    exact ⟨⟨inferInstance, inferInstance⟩, inferInstance⟩
263	  rw [Category.assoc, hV.specMap_quotient_mk_fromSpec_over] at hfin
264	  exact RingHom.finite_algebraMap.mp ((IsFinite.SpecMap_iff _).mp hfin)
265	
266	end IsAffineOpen
267	
268	/-! ## The adaptation corollaries: the (c1)-finite clause per piece -/
269	
270	section Adaptation
271	
272	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} [IsProper C.hom]
273	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
274	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k}
275	
276	namespace DivisorAdaptation
277	
278	variable [IsFinite π] {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
279	variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d)
280	
281	/-- **The (c1)-finite clause from a closed support trace** (the core adaptation
282	corollary): if the piece trace of the family support is closed in the relative curve,
283	the chart-local colength `Γ(D(h_j)) ⧸ (f_j)` is a finite `R`-module — the
284	`IsCertified.finite_colength` clause at `j`, and the `[Module.Finite]` input of the
285	landed `projective_colength_of_forall_tmul_residueField`.  Consumes the properness
286	licence (`instIsProperRelCurveHom`); no Noetherian hypothesis. -/
287	theorem finite_colength_of_isClosed_supportLocus_inter (j : A.index)
288	    (hclosed : IsClosed (d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)))) :
289	    Module.Finite R (A.colength j) := by
290	  rw [A.supportLocus_inter_pieces j] at hclosed
291	  exact (A.toFinCoverData.isAffineOpen_pieces j).finite_quotient_span_singleton_of_isClosed
292	    (A.eqn j) hclosed
293	
294	/-- The (c1)-finite clause in the leak-locus spelling: nothing leaks out of the piece
295	`j`, so the trace is closed and the colength is finite. -/
296	theorem finite_colength_of_supportLeak_eq_empty (j : A.index)
297	    (hleak : d.supportLeak (A.pieces j) = ∅) :
298	    Module.Finite R (A.colength j) :=
299	  A.finite_colength_of_isClosed_supportLocus_inter j
300	    ((d.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty (A.pieces j)).mpr hleak)
301	
302	/-- **The (c1)-finite clause from fibrewise no-leak data** (the CertUniv threading
303	slot): if over every base point the fibre of the closure of the piece trace stays in
304	the piece — the topological shadow of the P-fib-N fibrewise finiteness data combined
305	with the seed design — then the colength of the piece `j` is a finite `R`-module. -/
306	theorem finite_colength_of_forall_fibre_closure_subset (j : A.index)
307	    (hfib : ∀ s : Spec (CommRingCat.of R),
308	      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).base ⁻¹' {s}
309	          ∩ closure (d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)))
310	        ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
311	    Module.Finite R (A.colength j) :=
312	  A.finite_colength_of_supportLeak_eq_empty j
313	    (d.supportLeak_eq_empty_of_forall_fibre
314	      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)) hfib)
315	
316	/-- The (c1)-finite clause when the piece dominates the support: if the whole family
317	support lies in the piece `j` (the shape the support tube produces after shrinking the
318	base), the colength is finite.  The fibrewise form `∀ s, fibre ∩ supportLocus ⊆ piece`
319	reduces to this hypothesis by `fun x hx => hfib _ ⟨rfl, hx⟩`. -/
320	theorem finite_colength_of_supportLocus_subset (j : A.index)
321	    (hsub : d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
322	    Module.Finite R (A.colength j) :=
323	  A.finite_colength_of_isClosed_supportLocus_inter j (by
324	    rw [Set.inter_eq_left.mpr hsub]
325	    exact d.isClosed_supportLocus)
326	
327	end DivisorAdaptation
328	
329	end Adaptation

331	end AlgebraicGeometry

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamily
import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.GluedSheafExtraction

/-!
# Finite-adaptation extraction: every local-equation system has a chart adaptation
(`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §3 stage (d))

Every `LocalEquations` system `d` on the relative curve `C_R = relCurve C R` refines to a
finite chart adaptation `DivisorAdaptation C R π d` (`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §1a): the two
pinned charts `V₀ᴿ`, `V₁ᴿ` are affine, so the DAT-1 (1f) affine-refinement engine
(`IsAffineOpen.exists_finite_basicOpen_refinement` in
`AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.GluedSheafExtraction`)
produces, for each chart, a finite basic-open family subordinated to `d.cover` at anchor
points, with a partition of unity. Reindexing each chart family through `Fintype.equivFin`
gives the `Fin`-indexed `FinCoverData`; the equations are the restrictions of `d`'s
equations at the anchors (comparison unit `1`), regular by `d.regular` through the
refinement subordination.

The **certificate** (`DivisorAdaptation.IsCertified`) is deliberately NOT part of the
extraction: an adaptation always exists, whereas the colength certificate is an extra
finiteness/flatness hypothesis on `d` (the object of DD-1c's field dictionary and DAT-B's
coverage step, which supply it separately).

* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_divisorAdaptation` — the extraction: `Nonempty
  (DivisorAdaptation C R π d)` for every `d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations`.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
variable (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsAffineHom π]

/-- **Finite-adaptation extraction** (`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §3 stage (d), the DAT-1 (1f)
pattern): every local-equation system on the relative curve refines to a finite chart
adaptation. The two pinned charts are affine, so on each the affine-refinement engine
produces a finite basic-open family subordinated to `d.cover` at anchor points with a
partition of unity; the equations are the anchor equations of `d` restricted to the pieces
(comparison unit `1`), regular through the subordination. The colength certificate is a
separate hypothesis and is not produced here. -/
theorem exists_divisorAdaptation (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) :
    Nonempty (DivisorAdaptation C R π d) := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨ι₀, _, f₀, an₀, b₀, hsub₀, hpart₀⟩ :=
    (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C R (fiberTwoCover π)).exists_finite_basicOpen_refinement d.cover
  obtain ⟨ι₁, _, f₁, an₁, b₁, hsub₁, hpart₁⟩ :=
    (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C R (fiberTwoCover π)).exists_finite_basicOpen_refinement d.cover
  set e₀ : Fin (Fintype.card ι₀) ≃ ι₀ := (Fintype.equivFin ι₀).symm with he₀
  set e₁ : Fin (Fintype.card ι₁) ≃ ι₁ := (Fintype.equivFin ι₁).symm with he₁
  -- the `Fin`-indexed cover data
  set D : FinCoverData C R π :=
    { m₀ := Fintype.card ι₀
      m₁ := Fintype.card ι₁
      h₀ := fun j => f₀ (e₀ j)
      h₁ := fun j => f₁ (e₁ j)
      a₀ := fun j => b₀ (e₀ j)
      a₁ := fun j => b₁ (e₁ j)
      partition₀ := (Equiv.sum_comp e₀ (fun i => b₀ i * f₀ i)).trans hpart₀
      partition₁ := (Equiv.sum_comp e₁ (fun i => b₁ i * f₁ i)).trans hpart₁ } with hD
  -- the anchor of each piece and its subordination to a member of `d.cover`
  set pt : D.index → relCurve C R :=
    Sum.elim (fun j => an₀ (e₀ j)) (fun j => an₁ (e₁ j)) with hpt
  have hle : ∀ j : D.index, D.pieces j ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j) := by
    rintro (j | j)
    · exact hsub₀ (e₀ j)
    · exact hsub₁ (e₁ j)

---
name: subagents
description: How the Horizon agent delegates to native subagents for review and upkeep — spawning by name, read-only enforcement, dispatch-time model choice, and the dynamic descriptor roster.
---

Subagents are **your team's workers**: focused helpers you (the team lead) spawn
to divide up review and upkeep while you keep proving. This is delegation
*within* your team and needs no permission — distinct from launching new tasks or
runs for *other* teams, which is off by default (see the `horizon` skill,
"Delegating beyond your team"). The `ground` helper is the fresh-context
checkpoint for workspace-wide strategy and hygiene; it is a subagent, not a
second orchestrator role.

Bundled descriptors and any workspace overrides under
`.archon-horizon/subagents/<name>.md` are merged at the start of every `horizon
run`, then compiled into your engine's **native** subagent format,
workspace-local:

- Claude Code → `.claude/agents/<name>.md`
- Codex → `.codex/agents/<name>.toml`

Use the engine's native roster, or list `.codex/agents/*.toml` for Codex and
`.claude/agents/*.md` for Claude, to see every runnable helper. Do not treat an
empty `.archon-horizon/subagents/` directory as an empty roster: that directory
holds workspace overrides/custom helpers only; built-ins such as `ground`,
`janitor`, and `work-reviewer` still appear in the compiled native directory.
Pick the right helper and scope from those generated descriptions.

## Dispatch

Spawn a subagent **by name** through your engine's own native subagent
mechanism, with a focused directive: the slice/scope (a chapter, a task, a
project) and the project it applies to. Spawn several in parallel when the work
divides cleanly, then wait for and reconcile their reports. Give one subagent
one scoped slice so the workspace scales to many projects.

Delegation is part of the normal workflow, not an exceptional recovery path.
For a session that touches more than one file, more than one proof obligation,
or is expected to run longer than ten minutes, dispatch at least one bounded
review/helper before the final report. On a multi-session task, dispatch
`ground` before the terminal completion claim and `janitor` at the scheduled
hygiene checkpoints. Use the engine's native `spawn_agent`/Task mechanism,
wait for the helper to finish, and reconcile its report in your own result. If
no suitable helper is available, state why delegation was skipped in the report.

## Read-only and write scope

A descriptor's `read_only: true` is compiled to real engine enforcement — Claude
`disallowedTools: [Edit, Write, NotebookEdit]`, Codex `sandbox_mode = "read-only"`
— so a read-only reviewer cannot edit source. Every subagent (read-only or not)
can still file issues/memory and write its report via the `horizon inbox` CLI;
that is how read-only agents act. The descriptor's `write_domain` documents what
a writer is expected to touch (Lean/blueprint/reference source).

## Model and effort — the Horizon agent owns the spend

Descriptors intentionally carry no model, tier, or effort setting. Generated
Claude/Codex descriptors inherit the parent session by default. At dispatch time,
the Horizon agent chooses the native model and reasoning effort for that helper:
use the same model/effort for mathematical review, a lighter capable option for
mechanical search/lint/hygiene, and a vision-capable option for page transcription.
If the engine cannot express a per-call override, inherit the parent and record
the choice in the report rather than hiding a model policy in `config.yaml`.

The same rule applies to a named subagent, a bare Task/Agent spawn, or any
workflow fan-out. Match model and effort to the actual slice, and before a large
fan-out check `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. If headroom is low, commit work in
flight first so an interruption loses nothing.

To add or change a subagent, edit its descriptor under
`.archon-horizon/subagents/` — it recompiles on the next run. Do not rely on a
stale hard-coded roster in this skill.

open scoped TensorProduct

/-! ## The topological tube core -/

section TubeCore

variable {X Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y]

/-- **The closed-map tube lemma**: for a closed map `f`, a closed `T ⊆ X` and an open
`U ⊆ X`, if the `T`-fibre over `y` is contained in `U` then so is `f⁻¹(V) ∩ T` for some
open neighbourhood `V` of `y`. Take `V := Set.kernImage f (U ∪ Tᶜ)`, open by
`isClosedMap_iff_kernImage`. -/
theorem IsClosedMap.exists_isOpen_preimage_inter_subset {f : X → Y}
    (hf : IsClosedMap f) {T U : Set X} (hT : IsClosed T) (hU : IsOpen U) {y : Y}
    (hfib : f ⁻¹' {y} ∩ T ⊆ U) :
    ∃ V : Set Y, IsOpen V ∧ y ∈ V ∧ f ⁻¹' V ∩ T ⊆ U := by
  refine ⟨Set.kernImage f (U ∪ Tᶜ),
    isClosedMap_iff_kernImage.mp hf (hU.union hT.isOpen_compl), ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro x hx
    by_cases hxT : x ∈ T
    · exact Or.inl (hfib ⟨hx, hxT⟩)
    · exact Or.inr hxT
  · rintro x ⟨hxV, hxT⟩
    rcases hxV (rfl : f x = f x) with h | h
    · exact h
    · exact absurd hxT h

end TubeCore

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

/-! ## The support locus of a local-equation system -/

namespace Scheme.LocalEquations

variable {X S : Scheme.{u}} (d : X.LocalEquations)

/-- **The unit locus** of a local-equation system: the (open) union of the basic opens
of the equations — the locus where the divisor cut by `d` is trivial. -/
def unitLocus : X.Opens := ⨆ x, X.basicOpen (d.eqn x)

lemma basicOpen_le_unitLocus (x : X) : X.basicOpen (d.eqn x) ≤ d.unitLocus :=
  le_iSup (fun x => X.basicOpen (d.eqn x)) x

/-- Membership in the unit locus reads on ANY covering member containing the point:
`y ∈ unitLocus` iff the germ of `eqn x` at `y` is a unit, for every member `x` with
`y ∈ cover.opens x` (well-definedness across members is the ratio law). -/
lemma mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ {x y : X} (hy : y ∈ d.cover.opens x) :
    y ∈ d.unitLocus
      ↔ IsUnit ((X.presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens x) y hy).hom (d.eqn x)) := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    obtain ⟨x', hx'⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp h
    have hy' : y ∈ d.cover.opens x' := X.basicOpen_le _ hx'
    have hu' : IsUnit ((X.presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens x') y hy').hom (d.eqn x')) :=
      (X.mem_basicOpen _ y hy').mp hx'
    obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := d.ratio_isUnit x x'
    have hyW : y ∈ d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens x' := ⟨hy, hy'⟩
    have h := congrArg
      ((X.presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens x') y hyW).hom) hu
    rw [map_mul, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply] at h
    rw [h, IsUnit.mul_iff]
    exact ⟨u.isUnit.map _, hu'⟩
  · intro h
    exact Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨x, (X.mem_basicOpen _ y hy).mpr h⟩

/-- **The support locus** of a local-equation system: the closed set of points where
the (well-defined) germ of the local equation fails to be a unit — the underlying set
of the divisor cut by `d`. -/
def supportLocus : Set X := (d.unitLocus : Set X)ᶜ

lemma isClosed_supportLocus : IsClosed d.supportLocus :=
  d.unitLocus.isOpen.isClosed_compl

lemma mem_supportLocus_iff_not_isUnit_germ {x y : X} (hy : y ∈ d.cover.opens x) :
    y ∈ d.supportLocus
      ↔ ¬ IsUnit ((X.presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens x) y hy).hom (d.eqn x)) :=
  not_congr (d.mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ hy)

/-- **The per-member trace of the support**: on a covering member, the support locus is
the member minus the basic open of its equation. -/
lemma supportLocus_inter_opens (x : X) :
    d.supportLocus ∩ (d.cover.opens x : Set X)
      = (d.cover.opens x : Set X) \ (X.basicOpen (d.eqn x) : Set X) := by
  ext y
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hsupp, hy⟩
    refine ⟨hy, fun hyb => hsupp (d.basicOpen_le_unitLocus x hyb)⟩
  · rintro ⟨hy, hyb⟩
    refine ⟨fun hyU => hyb ?_, hy⟩
    exact (X.mem_basicOpen _ y hy).mpr ((d.mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ hy).mp hyU)

/-- **The support is closed over the base**: the image of the support locus under a
universally closed morphism (e.g. the structure morphism of the relative curve, from
the standing `IsProper C.hom`) is closed. -/
theorem isClosed_image_supportLocus (f : X ⟶ S) [UniversallyClosed f] :
    IsClosed (f.base '' d.supportLocus) :=
  f.isClosedMap _ d.isClosed_supportLocus

/-- **The support tube** (piece isolation, Zariski-locally on the base): for a
universally closed `f : X ⟶ S`, if the support fibre over a base point `s` is contained
in an open `U` (a union of adaptation pieces, in the DDR-4 instantiation), then there
is a Zariski neighbourhood `V` of `s` such that the whole support over `V` is contained
in `U`. -/
theorem exists_supportTube (f : X ⟶ S) [UniversallyClosed f] {U : Set X}
    (hU : IsOpen U) {s : S} (hfib : f.base ⁻¹' {s} ∩ d.supportLocus ⊆ U) :
    ∃ V : S.Opens, s ∈ V ∧ f.base ⁻¹' (V : Set S) ∩ d.supportLocus ⊆ U := by
  obtain ⟨V, hVopen, hsV, hV⟩ := (f.isClosedMap).exists_isOpen_preimage_inter_subset
    d.isClosed_supportLocus hU hfib
  exact ⟨⟨V, hVopen⟩, hsV, hV⟩

end Scheme.LocalEquations

THE seam brick of the DD-R endgame (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` §3 item 4, probe verdict
GREEN): the bridge between DD-1's `gluedSubmodule`-style carriers and the rigid engine's
Čech `H⁰` of the constructed family's twisted glued sheaf.  For a divisor family `d`
with finite chart adaptation `A` on the relative curve `C_R` and a twist exponent `a`,
the global sections of the theta-ideal datum sheaf (`DivisorAdaptation.thetaIdealDatum`,
the engine-ready presentation of `𝒪(Θᵃ − d)`) are identified `R`-linearly with the
vanishing submodule `K_a(d) = H⁰(𝒪(Θᵃ − d)) ⊆ H⁰(𝒪(Θᵃ))`:

* `DivisorAdaptation.vanishingSide` / `vanishingDiv` — a global twisted pair vanishing
  along `d`, read on the piece `D(h_p)` through its pinned-chart side, and its unique

/-!
# Finiteness of adaptation overlap colengths

If the support traces on adaptation pieces do not leak, then the trace on a pairwise
overlap is the intersection of two closed traces.  The overlap ideal is principal by
`DivisorAdaptation.ovlIdeal_eq_span_left`, so the proper affine finiteness engine applies
to every overlap colength and hence to their finite product.
-/

/-- A ring equivalence carries nonzerodivisors to nonzerodivisors. -/
private lemma ringEquiv_mem_nonZeroDivisors {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    (e : A ≃+* B) {x : A} (hx : x ∈ nonZeroDivisors A) :
    e x ∈ nonZeroDivisors B := by
  rw [mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff] at hx ⊢
  obtain ⟨hl, hr⟩ := hx
  constructor
  · intro y hy
    have h := congrArg e.symm hy
    rw [map_mul, map_zero, e.symm_apply_apply] at h
    have hy0 : e.symm y = 0 := hl _ h
    calc y = e (e.symm y) := (e.apply_symm_apply y).symm
      _ = 0 := by rw [hy0, map_zero]
  · intro y hy
    have h := congrArg e.symm hy
    rw [map_mul, map_zero, e.symm_apply_apply] at h
    have hy0 : e.symm y = 0 := hr _ h
    calc y = e (e.symm y) := (e.apply_symm_apply y).symm
      _ = 0 := by rw [hy0, map_zero]

/-- Closed support traces on two pieces make their overlap colength finite over the
base. -/
theorem finite_ovlColength_of_isClosed_supportLocus_inter (i j : A.index)
    (hi : IsClosed (d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces i : Set (relCurve C R))))
    (hj : IsClosed (d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)))) :
    Module.Finite R (A.ovlColength i j) := by
  let V : (relCurve C R).Opens := A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j
  let f : Γ(relCurve C R, V) :=
    (relCurve C R).resHom
      (inf_le_left : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces i) (A.eqn i)
  have hclosed : IsClosed ((V : Set (relCurve C R)) \
      ((relCurve C R).basicOpen f : Set (relCurve C R))) := by
    have heq : ((V : Set (relCurve C R)) \
          ((relCurve C R).basicOpen f : Set (relCurve C R))) =
        (d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces i : Set (relCurve C R))) ∩
          (d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) := by
      rw [show (relCurve C R).basicOpen f =
        V ⊓ (relCurve C R).basicOpen (A.eqn i) from
          Scheme.basicOpen_resHom inf_le_left (A.eqn i)]
      ext x
      have htrace := Set.ext_iff.mp (A.supportLocus_inter_pieces i) x
      simp only [Set.mem_sdiff, SetLike.mem_coe, Opens.mem_inf, Set.mem_inter_iff] at htrace ⊢
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨hxV, hxnot⟩
        have hsi : x ∈ d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces i : Set (relCurve C R)) :=
          htrace.mpr ⟨hxV.1, fun hxi => hxnot ⟨hxV, hxi⟩⟩
        exact ⟨hsi, hsi.1, hxV.2⟩
      · rintro ⟨hsi, _, hxj⟩
        have hdiff := htrace.mp hsi
        exact ⟨⟨hsi.2, hxj⟩, fun hx => hdiff.2 hx.2⟩
    rw [heq]
    exact hi.inter hj
  have hVaff : IsAffineOpen V := by
    rw [show V = (relCurve C R).basicOpen (A.toFinCoverData.ovlGen i j) from
      (A.toFinCoverData.basicOpen_ovlGen i j).symm]
    exact (A.toFinCoverData.isAffineOpen_preimage_chart_inf R i j).basicOpen _
  have hfin := hVaff.finite_quotient_span_singleton_of_isClosed (R := R) f hclosed
  have hideal := A.ovlIdeal_eq_span_left i j
  change A.ovlIdeal i j = Ideal.span {f} at hideal
  letI : Module.Finite R (Γ(relCurve C R, V) ⧸ Ideal.span {f}) := hfin
  exact Module.Finite.equiv
    ((Submodule.quotEquivOfEq _ _ hideal).symm.restrictScalars R)

        ⊆ (A.pieces l : Set (relCurve C R))) :
    Module.Finite R (A.ovlColength i j) := by
  apply A.finite_ovlColength_of_isClosed_supportLocus_inter i j

noncomputable abbrev colength (j : A.index) : Type u :=

/-- The symmetric overlap ideal: both equations restricted to the piece overlap. The
two restrictions generate the same ideal (the equations differ by units on overlaps
through the refinement witness), but the symmetric span needs no transport in the
DEFINITION. -/
noncomputable abbrev ovlIdeal (i j : A.index) :
    Ideal Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) :=
  Ideal.span
